questions.cardText:
[Musicology] What letter does the treble clef symbol represent?
A. G
B. E
C. C
Answer: A. The treble clef is also known as the G clef because it spirals around the second line of the staff, which represents the note G.
questions.de: Welchen Ton legt der Violinschlüssel auf der zweiten Notenlinie fest, nach dem er auch benannt ist?
questions.en: Which note does the treble clef fix on the second line of the staff, giving it its other name?

timeline.labelEn: Guido of Arezzo develops staff notation, whose lines were labelled with key-letters F, C or G, the origin of clefs
timeline.labelDe: Guido von Arezzo entwickelt die Liniennotation, deren Linien mit Schlüsselbuchstaben F, C oder G bezeichnet wurden, dem Ursprung der Schlüssel

questions.notes: Wikipedia (Clef): the treble clef is a G-clef placing G4 on the second line of the staff. Clefs began as key-letters (F, C, G) on chant staff lines (Clef, History); timeline from Guido of Arezzo's 11th-century staff notation (Wikipedia, Guido of Arezzo), approximate.

questions.cardText:
[History] Which of the following was NOT commonly used by Viking warriors in battle?
A. Axe
B. Horned helmets
C. Spear
Answer: B. There is limited historical evidence that Viking warriors wore any horned helmets in battle. The image of horned helmets was mostly popularized by 19th-century opera costumes.
questions.de: Welche Kopfbedeckung, die durch Kostüme für Wagners Opern im 19. Jahrhundert populär wurde, trugen Wikingerkrieger in Wirklichkeit nicht im Kampf?
questions.en: What headgear, popularized by costumes for Wagner's operas in the 19th century, did Viking warriors not actually wear in battle?

timeline.labelEn: Carl Emil Doepler's horned-helmet costumes for Wagner's Ring cycle at Bayreuth start the horned-Viking myth
timeline.labelDe: Carl Emil Doeplers Hörnerhelm-Kostüme für Wagners „Ring“ in Bayreuth begründen den Mythos der gehörnten Wikinger

questions.notes: Card says 'limited historical evidence'; Wikipedia (Horned helmet, Carl Emil Doepler) says it is merely a modern association with no direct archaeological evidence, started by Doepler's 1876 Bayreuth costumes for Wagner's Ring.
